newsitem.title: INDIA: India IOC says 100-bln rupee investments in works.
newsitem.headline: India IOC says 100-bln rupee investments in works.

text.p: State-run Indian Oil Corp (IOC) said on Tuesday it had current projects involving an investment of 100 billion rupees and planned to invest 250 billion rupees in other projects in the future.

"Projects of about 100 billion rupees are in hand and investments of over 250 billion rupees have been identified," the Fortune 500 company, which owns six refineries and some 5,300 km of land pipelines in India, said in a statement.
"Indian Oil has decided to globalise its operations," chairman R.K. Narang told a news conference in New Delhi after its annual meeting on Monday.
The investments involve the building of new refineries, expansion of existing refineries, pipelines, terminals, storage depots and ancillary facilities for oil products.
The ongoing projects include a 6.0 million tonnes per annum capacity refinery in the northern city of Panipat which Narang said would be completed in 1997/98.
The project involves an investment of 38.68 billion rupees and is proposed to be later expanded later by three million tonnes at an investment of 27.65 billion rupees.

Among the other proposed investments are one to build a giant grassroots refinery in the eastern coastal town of Paradeep in collaboration with Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC), involving an investment of more than 100 billion rupees.
Narang said the 12 million tonnes per annum capacity refinery was expected to be completed by 2000.
IOC and KPC will hold 26 percent each in the joint venture, and the rest would be sold to the public or placed privately to other investors, IOC said in a statement.
"It is also proposed to set up a product pipeline from this refinery to high consumption centres," the statement said.

IOC said it recently got a contract to operate an oil terminal in Zambia and launched its servo lubricants in Nepal. It plans to introduce the lubricants in Dubai and other parts of the United Arab Emirates, the statement said.
IOC has signed memoranda of understanding with Petronas group of Malaysia and Japan's Marubeni group to form joint ventures, details of which are yet to be worked out, it said.

Indian Oil closed 1995/96 (April-March) with a turnover of 438.62 billion rupees and a profit after tax of 12.49 billion rupees. Senior company officials expect the net profit to rise to around 18 billion rupees in 1996/97.
Product sales were at 39.85 million tonnes in 1995/96, throughput of refineries at 25.64 million tonnes and throughput in pipelines at 24.70 million tonnes, the statement said.
